newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares remain weaker in uncertain trade.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares remain weaker in uncertain trade.

text.p: Swedish shares remained weaker early afternoon Thursday in uncertain, light trade with market heavyweight Ericsson leading the slump.
The Stockholm general index slipped 0.26 percent to 3,182.96, falling off Wednesday's record high close, in light, summer trade with shares worth 1.47 billion crowns swapped.
"Everyone is sitting on the fence and waiting to see which way the market will go," said one broker. "There is some concern about a recoil in the U.S.."
Telecoms Ericsson fell 4.5 to 362.5 crowns which brokers attributed to some profittaking.
The other market heavyweight, drugs major Astra, fell two to 146 crowns.

U.S./Swedish drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn slumped eight to 295.5 crowns after posting a worse than expected second quarter result on Tuesday which prompted analysts to again downgrade their forecasts for the company.
"I think that P&U will come back up again once the U.S. market starts trading this afternoon," one broker said.
U.S. credit rating agency Moody's upgraded the ratings of two insurance companies, Trygg-Hansaand Skandia. Both were raised to A3 from Baa1.
Trygg-Hansa rose 3.5 crowns to 158.5 while Skandia fell five to 325 crowns.
Trade was lively in computer company Lap Powerm that rose 2.20 crowns to 16.10 after reporting computer sales increased by 60 percent between May and July to 6,600 computers against a year ago.
